Standard: The AR system interface, its attachment to airframe structure, and the structure surrounding the interface do not fail (experience permanent deformation) prior to the ultimate loads that can be generated during the AR process. a. Boom Tanker. Boom ultimate design loads: 1. 16,166 lbs tension, boom fully extended. 2. 7,500 lbs compression, boom not fully retracted. 3. 20,000 lbs compression, boom fully retracted. b. Drogue Tanker. Refueling hose ultimate design load is 2.5X the DLL. c. Receptacle Receiver. Receptacle ultimate design loads: 1. Tension: a load of 14,000/(Cos A) lbs applied to the boom-nozzle ball joint, where the angle A may vary from 0 degrees to 30 degrees and is relative to the receptacle axis. 2. Compression: a load of 20,000 lbs applied at the boom-nozzle ball joint anywhere within a 34-degree cone. 3. Slipway and its doors in both the open and closed positions, 2,000 lbs laterally and 5,000 lbs vertically. d. Probe Receiver. Probe attachment and surrounding structure withstand at least 1.5X probe DLLs. Probe tip and mast ultimate strength is greater than probe DLLs and less than support structure ultimate strength to ensure probe fails prior to attachment and support structure. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Structural analysis verifies boom structure and its attachment to the air vehicle do not fail prior to the required ultimate loads. b. Drogue Tanker. Structural loads analysis verifies refueling hose will not fail prior to the required ultimate loads. c. Receptacle Receiver. Structural loads analysis verifies that the receptacle, installation, and surrounding structure do not fail prior to the required ultimate loads. d. Probe Receiver. Structural loads analysis verifies that the probe tip and mast, attachment and surrounding structure do not fail prior to the required ultimate loads and the refueling probe fails prior to the attachment structure. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Static load laboratory testing of the boom system verifies boom components and structure do not fail prior to ultimate loads. b. Drogue Tanker. Static load laboratory testing verifies refueling hose does not fail prior to ultimate load. c. Receptacle Receiver. Static load laboratory testing on representative receptacle and surrounding structure verifies receptacle, attachment, and supporting structure does not fail prior to ultimate load. d. Probe Receiver. Static load laboratory testing on representative probe and attachment structure verifies attachment and surrounding structure does not fail prior to ultimate load and refueling probe fails prior to attachment structure. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight testing, including contacts, disconnects, pressure refueling, tension disconnects, and slipway assisted contacts with and without crewmember input, show boom system does not fail or deform during AR operations. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight testing including hose extension and retraction, receiver contacts at closure rates up to 10 ft/s and disconnects throughout the airspeed and altitude refueling envelope verify hose reel system and refueling assembly (fuel reception coupling and drogue) do not fail or deform during refueling operations. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight testing including contacts, disconnects, pressure refueling, tension disconnects, and slipway assisted contacts with and without crewmember input show that the receptacle does not fail or deform. d. Probe Receiver. Flight testing including contacts at closure rates up to 10 ft/s verify probe system and support structure do not fail or deform.
